newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse opens year in cautious trading.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse opens year in cautious trading.

text.p: Activity at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) was moderate on Thursday as investors traded cautiously reflecting a wait-and-see attitude, brokers said.
"Right now nobody really knows exactly what direction the market is going to take," one broker said, referring to this year's General elections.
"People are anticipating heavy campaign spending, so they'd rather sit on the fence," he added.
The index was up 1.71 points to stand at 3115.82 points. Turnover was posted at 14.799 million shillings traded on 267,201 shares from 10.814 million shillings traded on 252,559 shares on Tuesday.
But some brokers felt that it was still too early to predict for sure the prevailing market mood.
In the Commercials CMC Holdings traded 69,600 shares at 65 unchanged on the one hour hold board. Uchumi Supermarket was stable at 53.50 unchanged, while Kenya Airways was unchanged at 8.55.
A broker said he expected foreign investor interest in the Supermarket chain as it was one of the best performing shares among the locally controlled companies foreigners are allowed to invest in.
There was a lot of demand for Barclays Bank and Standard Chartered Bank. Barclays closed at 100 from 99.50 while Standard Chartered eased to 48.25 from 48.50.
A lot of excitement is developing around the financials as investors anticipate good company results sometime in February from almost all financial institutions.
Brokers said speculation revolved around the three leading banks, Standard Chartered, Barclays Bank and Kenya Commercial Bank.
"Barclays has been the traditional leader, but last year Kenya Commercial entered the market, the scene might change," one broker said.
Elsewhere, Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 10 from 9.75 while Bamburi Cement gained 50 cents to close at 65.50.
Foreigners bought 5,000 shares of Lonrho Motors at 128 from 129.
